newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's zinc shares outperform limp market.
newsitem.headline: Spain's zinc shares outperform limp market.

text.p: Spain's zinc shares marched higher on Tuesday, outperforming a generally weak market as buoyant zinc prices and a strong dollar boosted their value, dealers said.

By 1100 GMT, Asturiana del Zinc had climbed 30 pesetas to 3,380 after touching a high of 3,440 earlier in the session. Espanola del Zinc gained 50 pesetas to 2,060, after touching 2,120, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was 1.05 percent down at 6,746.35.

"The price of zinc, together with the strength of the dollar and taking into account that both companies basically sell in dollars have supported the price of both shares," said Agustin del Valle, analyst at Beta Capital brokerage.
"The price of zinc has risen by more than 10 percent in three days, and although it is falling today, the fundamentals for zinc remain very positive in the medium term," he added.
Zinc prices soared to seven-year highs of $1,674 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange on Monday, but on Tuesday, they crumbled to around $1,500.
Some analysts said Asturiana was the more attractive of the two Spanish firms, being backed by strong fundamentals.

However, some traders said Asturiana's stock price could find it difficult to strongly break the 3,400 level, the price which Glencore said it would pay for a 20 percent stake in the zinc producer earlier this month.
Some analysts said Glencore may now be forced to raise its offer. "It appears that now Glencore will have to stop its offer or make an offer with a higher price," said one.
But one dealer said if the firm wished to raise its offer it may have to wait for some time because of the legal restrictions of the deal.
No one at Asturiana was available to comment.
Glencore already holds a 24.79 percent stake in Asturiana.
